title: Guests report unexplained 'presences' during ghost hunt at historic Weston hotel
excerpt: Guests reported unexplained ‘presences’ during a ghost hunt at The Royal Hotel in Weston-super-Mare, which dates back more than 200 years
content:
Guests at a Weston-super-Mare hotel reported sensing mysterious “presences” during a paranormal investigation.

The ghost hunt took place at The Royal Hotel, where participants explored darkened rooms, vacant bedrooms and cellars.

Several guests described unusual feelings and experiences they said they could not explain.

The Royal Hotel hosted the paranormal investigation (Image: Google)

The hotel said: “What made the evening even more interesting was hearing how many people felt they weren’t quite alone.

“Several guests mentioned sensing presences, unusual feelings and experiences they couldn’t quite explain.

“And when you consider the history of our beautiful building, it certainly makes you wonder.”

The event followed a mystery tour before participants began investigating reports of unexplained activity at the South Parade hotel.

Organisers had previously stressed there would be no actors hiding around corners, staged scares or manufactured paranormal activity.

They also made clear before the event that there was no guarantee guests would experience anything paranormal.

Following the investigation, the hotel has asked former guests, visitors and employees to share any unexplained experiences of their own.

Guests reported ‘presences’ during the ghost hunt (Image: Google)

It said: “Have you ever stayed with us, worked here or visited The Royal Hotel and experienced something you couldn’t explain?

“Perhaps you’ve felt a presence, heard an unusual noise, seen something strange or simply had that feeling that someone was watching you?

“We’d love to hear your stories, whether they’re from recently or many years ago.”

The Grade II-listed hotel dates from the early 19th century and is believed to have been built between 1807 or 1808 and 1810.

Historic England describes it as Weston’s first hotel and says it was substantially enlarged around 1850.

Historical accounts say it was built on the site of an old farmhouse destroyed by fire in 1792.

It was initially known as The Hotel and was later associated with the names Fry’s Hotel and Reeve’s Hotel.

The hotel said generations of guests, employees and celebrations had passed through the building during its long history.

It added: “Over 200 years of history, but is everyone who checked in really gone?”
